BiblicalUsage: A cry for help goes up and is heard. The men of Ashdod cried until the cry of the city went up to heaven, David cried to his God in distress and his cry entered into God's ears, and Jeremiah hears the voice of the cry of the daughter of His people from a far country. Lamentations says plainly, Thou hast heard my voice: hide not thine ear at my cry.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the cry is the prayer God never misses. It rises from a plague-struck city and from a king in distress, and I hold that He hears it before the words are finished.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
